title: Flat diagonal and Tor groups
statement:
If $A\to B$ is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], then for
$B$-modules $M,N$ there are natural identifications

$$
 \operatorname{Tor}^B_i(M,N)=
 B\otimes_{B\otimes_AB}\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M,N).
$$

In particular, a common bound on the flat resolution lengths of all
$A$-modules is also such a bound for $B$-modules.

proof.text: Write $T=B\otimes_A B$ and $\mu:T\to B$, $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto b_1b_2$. All rings are commutative and all homological degrees are nonnegative. Construct a free $B$-resolution $P_\bullet\to M$: $P_0$ is the free module on the underlying set of $M$, mapping its basis element $[m]$ to $m$; Set $L_0=\ker(P_0\to M)$. Recursively, $P_{j+1}$ is free on the underlying set of $L_j$, the surjection $P_{j+1}\to L_j$ maps $[x]$ to $x$, and $L_{j+1}$ is its kernel. The differential $P_{j+1}\to P_j$ is that surjection followed by the inclusion $L_j\hookrightarrow P_j$. Thus its image equals the kernel of the preceding differential (or augmentation at $j=0$), so the augmented complex is exact. This works for arbitrary modules, including the zero module, without a finite generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 00LY (section-tor), free resolution; the free-on-elements construction writes out its existence

proof.text: By the weakly etale hypothesis $B$ is flat over $A$ and is flat over $T$ via $\mu$. Each $P_j\cong B^{(I_j)}$ is flat over $A$: for an exact sequence $U\to V\to W$ of $A$-modules, its tensor with $B$ is exact by the flat-tensor-exact node; its direct sum over $I_j$ remains exact, since every element has finite support and preimages can be chosen for its finitely many coordinates. The canonical identification $B^{(I_j)}\otimes_A U\cong (B\otimes_A U)^{(I_j)}$ sends $e_i b\otimes u$ to the $i$-th coordinate $b\otimes u$, with inverse the sum of these coordinate inclusions. Hence $P$ is an $A$-flat resolution. Put $C=P_\bullet\otimes_A N$, with the $T$-action $(b_1\otimes b_2)(p\otimes n)=b_1p\otimes b_2n$; the differentials are $T$-linear.

There is a canonical natural $T$-linear identification $H_i(C)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M,N)$, not merely an isomorphism of underlying groups. To verify it and its naturality, take a free $A$-resolution $Q\to N$ by the construction of step 1 and form $D_{j,k}=P_j\otimes_A Q_k$, with horizontal differential $d_P\otimes1$ and vertical differential $1\otimes d_Q$. On a pure tensor their two composites both give $d_P(p)\otimes d_Q(q)$, and each differential squares to zero; hence this is the commuting double complex required by the cited node. Its rows are exact in positive degrees because each $Q_k$ is flat, and its columns are exact in positive degrees because each $P_j$ is $A$-flat (step 2); use flat-tensor-exact in both cases. Tensor-right-exact identifies its row-cokernel complex with $M\otimes_A Q$ via $p\otimes q\mapsto\varepsilon_P(p)\otimes q$, and its column-cokernel complex with $P\otimes_A N$ via $p\otimes q\mapsto p\otimes\varepsilon_Q(q)$. The functorial double-complex-cokernel-homology isomorphism identifies their homologies. The factor swap $m\otimes q\mapsto q\otimes m$, the definition of Tor using $Q$, and Tor symmetry identify the former homology with $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(M,N)$. For $B$-linear maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, free modules are projective, so the projective-resolution-lift node gives a $B$-linear lift $a:P\to P'$ of $f$ and an $A$-linear lift $b:Q\to Q'$ of $g$. The maps $a_j\otimes b_k$ commute with both differentials; the displayed augmentation formulas show that they induce $f\otimes b$ and $a\otimes g$ on the two cokernel complexes. Functoriality of the double-complex isomorphism, the Tor-map-via-resolution-lift node, and naturality of Tor symmetry prove the claimed naturality, independent of the lifts. In particular apply this to multiplication by each $b_1$ on $M$ and each $b_2$ on $N$: these are $B$-linear maps, lifted on $P$ by multiplication and on $Q$ by a resolution lift. Thus the comparison intertwines both commuting $B$-actions, giving exactly the stated $T$-linearity.

proof.text: Because $B$ is $T$-flat, the canonical map $B\otimes_T H_i(C)\to H_i(B\otimes_T C)$, $b\otimes[z]\mapsto[b\otimes z]$, is an isomorphism. Explicitly put $Z_i=\ker d_i$ and $J_i=\operatorname{im}d_{i+1}$. Tensor the short exact sequences $0\to Z_i\to C_i\to J_{i-1}\to0$ and $0\to J_i\to Z_i\to H_i(C)\to0$ using flat-tensor-exact and tensor-right-exact. The injection $J_{i-1}\to C_{i-1}$ remains injective, so the new cycles are $B\otimes_T Z_i$. The surjection $C_{i+1}\to J_i$ remains surjective and the injection $J_i\to C_i$ remains injective, so the new boundaries are $B\otimes_T J_i$. The second sequence identifies their quotient with $B\otimes_T H_i(C)$. For $i=0$ take $C_{-1}=J_{-1}=0$. All inclusions and quotient maps commute with chain maps, so this isomorphism is natural.

source.place: Tags 00HB, 00HD; kernel/image/quotient argument for flat tensor and homology written explicitly

proof.text: There is a chain isomorphism $B\otimes_T(P_\bullet\otimes_A N)\cong P_\bullet\otimes_B N$, with degreewise map $b\otimes(p\otimes n)\mapsto bp\otimes n$ and inverse $p\otimes n\mapsto1\otimes(p\otimes n)$. The first map is $T$-balanced: acting by $b_1\otimes b_2$ on the second factor gives $bb_1p\otimes b_2n=bb_1b_2p\otimes n$, equal to its action through $\mu$ on the first factor. The inverse is $B$-balanced because $1\otimes(b p\otimes n)=b\otimes(p\otimes n)=1\otimes(p\otimes b n)$, using the two elements $b\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b$ of $T$. The two maps are inverse on pure tensors, commute with differentials, and commute with maps $a\otimes g$ from step 3. Since $P$ is a free $B$-resolution, its tensor with $N$ computes $\operatorname{Tor}^B_i(M,N)$ by the Tor definition. Combining steps 3 and 4 with this chain isomorphism yields the displayed formula as a natural $B$-module isomorphism. Naturality on the $B$-Tor side is precisely the Tor-map-via-resolution-lift statement applied to $a$ and $g$.

proof.text: For each j > d and B-modules M,N, choose the bounded flat A-resolution supplied by hA for the restricted M. Apply ModuleCat.flatResolution_torComparison to identify base Tor with the homology of its tensor with the restricted N. The term in degree j is zero, hence its tensor and its homology are zero. The first conclusion of this node (ModuleCat.exists_weaklyEtale_tor_iso, whose original hole remains open) identifies B-Tor with the diagonal scalar extension of this zero base-Tor module. The underlying group is subsingleton for every coefficient action; extendScalars preserves zero objects. Transport across the comparison to obtain the required B-Tor vanishing.

Apply the generic uniform Tor-vanishing-to-flat-resolution theorem [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-tor-bounded-resolution] to the lifted ring B and bound d, using the vanishing just proved. All coefficient rings and module universes are the same canonical ULifts as in the original statement.
